issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC regex in font-weight-notation only matches 400/700, missing other numeric weights
issues.detail: The regex is built from NUMERIC_TO_NAMED.keys() which contains only '400' and '700'. For primary='named-where-possible', a value like 'font-weight: 500' would skip processing. This is likely intentional (only those map to names), but worth confirming no existing warning path handles non-mappable numeric weights — otherwise behavior silently changes.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks anchor for end-of-string and may miss valid selectors
issues.detail: The regex `(?:^|[,\s])(?:${selectors})` matches the start of percentage tokens but assumes PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS entries include their '%' suffix. If any entry is like '0' without '%', the regex would falsely match decimals in unrelated text. Verify entries are normalized; consider adding a trailing word boundary or '%' anchor for safety.

issues.description: Hardcoded `url(` regex in import-notation ignores CSS escape sequences and case-only matching nuance
issues.detail: The check `/url\(/i.test(params)` would miss escaped forms like `\url(` (uncommon but valid CSS) and any whitespace between identifier and paren (e.g., `url (`) which CSS technically rejects but tokenizers may normalize. Aligns with valueParser but edge cases may diverge from prior behavior.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation prefix regex `/[<>]/` could match inside string values
issues.detail: If atRule.params contains a quoted string or comment with `<` or `>` characters (rare but possible in custom media or strange syntax), the regex would still trigger processing rather than skip. Not a correctness regression (it just defeats the optimization in that edge case), but worth a brief comment.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element walkRules(/:/) may match attribute selectors with namespace prefix
issues.detail: A selector like `[xml\:lang]` contains a literal `:` inside an attribute selector and would pass the walkRules filter unnecessarily. Not a bug — the inner parser still rejects non-pseudo cases — but the filter is slightly looser than the prior `selector.includes(':')` check (which was identical). Equivalent behavior; flagging for awareness only.

issues.description: No tests added for the new early-exit paths
issues.detail: The diff modifies hot paths in six rules without adding regression tests asserting that filtered-out declarations/rules still produce no warnings (and that the original warning behavior is preserved for the inverse). Existing tests likely cover positive cases, but a quick test confirming, e.g., `font-weight: 400` with primary='numeric' produces zero warnings and triggers no inner work would lock in the optimization intent.

review.summary: This PR adds early-exit regex checks to six `*-notation` rules to skip expensive AST parsing when no relevant tokens exist. The optimization is sound and well-targeted, but a few regexes have subtle assumptions worth verifying: HAS_NUMERIC in font-weight only covers the two mapped values (400/700), HAS_PERCENTAGE in keyframe-selector assumes selectors include the `%` suffix, and the prefix/url checks could be evaded by edge cases inside strings. None are clear correctness bugs — the inner logic remains the source of truth — but adding regression tests for the new fast-paths would lock in the intended behavior. No P0 issues found.
